pron_note: Written in ordinary Norwegian spelling, not phonetic symbols. When a word is not stressed on its first syllable, a mark after the stressed syllable shows where the stress falls, and which of Norwegian's two word melodies it has: ˊ for tone 1, ˋ for tone 2. The two tones can tell apart words that are otherwise said alike, such as bønder, 'farmers' (tone 1), and bønner, 'beans' (tone 2). How they sound depends on the dialect: in Eastern Norwegian, as in Oslo, tone 1 starts low on the stressed syllable and rises, while tone 2 falls on the stressed syllable before it rises. A hyphen means only part of the word is spelt out.

settings.applied: Changes apply at once and are kept in this browser.
settings.colour.hint: The colour of links, headings, buttons and the sense numbers.
settings.defs.en.note: Shows only the English of each definition: the shortest articles, for when you only need the meaning. Set phrases not yet translated are left out. An article not yet translated still shows its Norwegian.
settings.defs.no: Norwegian, with the English hidden until revealed
settings.defs.no.note: For when you mostly follow the Norwegian: each definition's English stays hidden until you click "Show English" under it; click the English again to hide it. The English glosses under the headword still show, and formula lines and the etymology follow their own settings.
settings.emph.en.note: In the example sentences, the Norwegian stays emphasized.
settings.emph.hint: Which line of a definition is in the full text colour; the other is faded, and its links are plain words. Not used when Definitions is "Norwegian, with the English hidden": there the Norwegian always leads.
settings.examples.no: Norwegian, with the English hidden until revealed
settings.examples.no.note: For practising your Norwegian: read the example first, then click "Show English" under it to check yourself.
settings.exeye: An eye button for the examples' English
settings.exeye.hint: On: an eye beside the headword hides the English of every example in the article, or shows it again, so you can switch between reading the Norwegian and checking yourself without opening Settings. While the English is hidden, "Show English" under an example reveals that one. The Examples setting above decides how an article opens.
settings.exlimit: Examples under each sense and set phrase
settings.exlimit.hint: Fewer examples make a long article quicker to skim. Each sense, subsense and set phrase shows its first examples, in the article's order, including the examples Ordpar has added (marked +). Small articles keep their own limit. With a number chosen, the next setting decides whether the rest can still be opened.
settings.exmore: A line to show the examples left out
settings.exmore.hint: On: where the setting above leaves examples out, a line such as "Show 12 more examples" at the end of those examples opens them in place. Off: they are not shown.
settings.formulas: Short formula lines, such as "used as an adverb:"
settings.formulas.both.note: The labels of compound lists and the words in a pronunciation stay in English.
settings.formulas.hint: On an article not yet translated, they are always in Norwegian.
settings.formulas.no.note: The labels of compound lists and the words in a pronunciation, such as "in the plural", are in Norwegian too.
settings.infl.open.note: The tables of a word's forms (hus, huset, husene …) show without clicking the Inflection button. Handy when you are learning the forms; the articles get longer.
settings.labels.hint: The headings and buttons inside an article, such as "Etymology" and "Copy link", its word class and the words of its inflection tables. With "Norwegian only" on, the word class and the inflection tables are in Norwegian whatever this says. The rest of the site, such as the header, the menus and Settings, stays in English.
settings.layout.ordbokene.note: Familiar if you use ordbokene.no: each numbered sense's own examples get an "Example" heading and line up with the definition above them, and no example list has the grey bar at its left.
settings.listview.hint: The list view shows each article the search finds as one short row (its headword, word class, whether it is translated, and its English glosses, or its Norwegian definition if not yet translated), which opens in place when clicked. Off: the articles the search finds as headwords are shown whole, one under another. Words found as an inflected form (such as huset, a form of hus) are always listed as links.
settings.listview.multi: Only when there are several articles
settings.listview.multi.note: Counts the articles found as headwords; words found as an inflected form don't count.
settings.mini.article.note: With Definitions set to "Norwegian, with the English hidden", a small article still shows its definitions in both languages, with nothing to click. Its examples, formula lines and etymology follow their own settings.
settings.mini.en.note: An article not yet translated is shown in Norwegian.
settings.minicontent: How much of the article it shows
settings.minicontent.full: In full: every subsense and compound list, and a few examples
settings.minicontent.hint: In both, each sense and subsense it shows that has examples gets its first one; more are then added one at a time, in turn, until there are 6 in all. With more than 6 senses and subsenses that have examples, each gets one.
settings.minicontent.slim: Shorter: some subsenses and compound lists left out
settings.minicontent.slim.note: Compound lists are left out wherever the sense or subsense has examples. And when the small article shows a whole word with several senses, a sense with its own definition is shown without its subsenses; a small article showing a single sense keeps them. To see everything, click the small article's headword: it opens the whole article.
settings.minifetch: When a linked article or page is loaded
settings.minifetch.click.note: Uses the least data: nothing is loaded before you click. An article can take a moment to open the first time.
settings.minifetch.hint: Loading an article or page before you open it makes it open faster, but uses data for the ones you never open. With the offline copy downloaded (Offline, below), articles come from the copy, so no data is used either way.
settings.minifetch.page.note: The fastest on a phone, which has no pointer to rest on. Uses the most data: the articles behind the page's links that open a small article, and the articles in a list view, are loaded with the page, whether you open them or not. Other links load as under "When the pointer rests on its link". With the browser's data saver on, only when the link is clicked.
settings.minifetch.point: When the pointer rests on its link
settings.minifetch.point.note: Articles and pages open almost at once on a computer. Uses a little extra data for links you rest on but don't click. On a touch screen, the article starts loading when you touch the link.
settings.minihw.article.note: It is still a link: click it to open the whole article.
settings.miniscroll: A long one, on a computer
settings.minitext.smaller.note: A step smaller than the article, so more of a long small article fits in its box.
settings.nbequiv.hidden.note: No English anywhere: not under the headword, not beside the words in the search suggestions, lists, Recent, History and Favourites, and not when the pointer rests on a linked word. The "Search English words" switch is hidden too, so the search and Random word are Norwegian; your choice on that switch comes back when you show the English again.
settings.nbequiv.shown.note: The short English equivalents stay under the headword and beside the words in the lists, and the "Search English words" switch stays. The articles themselves are still in Norwegian only.
settings.nbhover: When the pointer rests on a linked word
settings.nbhover.nbdef: The linked word's first Norwegian definition
settings.nbicon: A button in the header for Norwegian only
settings.nbicon.hint: On: a button beside Favourites and Settings (on a phone, beside "Search English words") switches Norwegian only on or off for every page, the same as the setting above, and this device keeps the choice until you press it again. Off: the setting above is the only way to switch it.
settings.nbonly: Show the articles in Norwegian only
settings.nbonly.hint: Shows every article in Norwegian only, with no English and nothing to click to reveal it. The Norwegian is Bokmålsordboka's article as it was in the copy Ordpar works from, with our corrections, so a change made at ordbokene.no since then may not be here yet. Your other settings are kept, and apply again when you switch this off.
settings.nbrows: Beside each word in the suggestions and lists
settings.nbrows.none.note: The words alone, as ordbokene.no's suggestions show them.
settings.nestminis: A link inside a small article
settings.nestminis.hint: In the same box: the box changes to the new word, and a line at its top, such as "← skip", goes back one word at a time. In a second box: the new small article opens below its word, over the first; a link inside the second box changes that box, with the same line back. In a box of its own: every link opens one more box, over the one before. There is no limit. A click outside every box closes them all.
settings.nestminis.inplace: Opens its small article in the same box
settings.nestminis.second: Opens its small article in a second box; a link there changes that box
settings.nestminis.stacked: Opens each small article in a box of its own
settings.noscript: The settings need JavaScript: they are kept in this browser's storage.
settings.peek: Translation when the pointer rests on a linked word
settings.peek.off.note: Fewer pop-ups while you read. A click still opens the link.
settings.pframes.hint: Grey helper words in a verb's inflection table that show how its perfect participle is used before a noun: "+ noun" after each form, and "den/det" before the definite form. Not shown in the narrower table used where the full one does not fit, as on a phone.
settings.popup: Copy the address for a pop-up dictionary
settings.popupNote: An address that opens Ordpar with your current settings, for a pop-up dictionary such as Definer. How to set one up: {link}.
settings.presets.intro: Each one sets all the article settings at once. Change any setting afterwards and your change stays. Your style, search and offline settings are not changed.
settings.presets.title: Presets
settings.resetNote: Puts every setting on this page back as Ordpar starts, your theme and colour too. To reset only the article settings, use Default at the top.
settings.stats.hint: Off: this browser sends none of the messages the Privacy page describes (page views, searches, suggestions chosen and installs). "Delete stored data" turns it back on.
settings.stored: Everything here is stored on this device only, and none of it is sent anywhere. No cookies, no accounts.
settings.sub.mini.intro: The box that opens on the page when you click a word linked to another article. It shows the word's senses only; click its headword for the whole article.
settings.sub.nbonly.intro: For reading the articles as Bokmålsordboka has them, with Ordpar's search, favourites and other features.
settings.subsenses.en.note: The subsenses marked with a bullet show only their English, so a long article is quicker to scan. Only when Definitions is "Norwegian and English"; short formula lines such as "used as an adverb:" have their own setting, below.
settings.suggestrows: Spacing of the suggestions under the search box

settings.xref.mini: Open as a small article on the page
